findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - unwrap on I/O result panics on file not found, permission denied, or unreadable paths
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path causes thread panic instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string is a filesystem I/O call embedded in the same function as parsing logic. I/O must be in the imperative shell; pure parsing must be in the functional core
findings.failure_mode: core calculation cannot be unit-tested without a real file on disk; side effects leak into deterministic logic
findings.fix: Split into two functions: a shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, E> that does fs::read_to_string, and a pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that handles parsing

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effecting I/O call inside the parsing core. Core calculations must be pure and deterministic with zero I/O
findings.failure_mode: purity invariant broken; core function behavior changes based on global stdout state; cannot be tested deterministically
findings.fix: Remove println entirely from core. If logging is needed, pass a logging callback or return a sequence of (Record, LogMessage) tuples from the shell layer

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> for every line. The grammar expects exactly two fields; split + collect is unnecessary allocation
findings.failure_mode: O(n) intermediate allocations per line where O(1) suffices; wasted heap memory and GC pressure
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get exactly (left, right) parts, then trim each side. No Vec or collect needed

findings.problem: parts[0] - unchecked array indexing without bounds check on a Vec produced from split. If the line has fewer than 1 comma-separated parts, this panics
findings.failure_mode: malformed input (empty line, single field) causes panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle the None case with map_err to return a ParseError; or use .get(0) with proper error handling

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - unwrap on parse panics on non-numeric value; also parts[1] is unchecked indexing
findings.failure_mode: malformed input (non-numeric second field, or line with only one field) causes thread panic; untrusted data aborts the function
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and unwrap_or_else/ok_or to produce a typed parse error. Replace unwrap with map_err returning a domain ParseError

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy width-reducing cast. Values > 65535 silently wrap, losing data without any indication
findings.failure_mode: out-of-range u32 values silently overflow to incorrect u16 values; data corruption with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and map_err the TryFromIntError. Or better: parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>() since the field type is u16

findings.problem: parts[1] - second unchecked array index. If line has only one comma-separated field, this panics
findings.failure_mode: malformed input causes panic instead of typed error
findings.fix: Replace split + collect with split_once(',') and handle missing second field via ok_or or unwrap_or_else

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() then cast to u16: wrong target type for a field that is u16. Should parse directly as u16
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary intermediate width + subsequent lossy cast chain increases chance of silent overflow
findings.fix: Use parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>() directly, with proper error handling

findings.problem: Return type Vec<Record> with no try_reserve. If the file is large, unbounded Vec growth can fail with OOM without any allocation error handling
findings.failure_mode: under memory pressure, Vec reallocation fails silently via panic (Vec grows by doubling without capacity checks)
findings.fix: Add a try_reserve hint or use Vec::with_capacity if count is known. At minimum, wrap in try_reserve in the shell layer before parsing loop

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), side effects (println), and data parsing in a single function. Violates functional core / imperative shell separation
findings.failure_mode: core parsing logic cannot be tested in isolation; testability degraded; purity invariant broken
findings.fix: Extract pure parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, RecordParseError> for the core. Shell function load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> handles I/O and delegates to core

findings.problem: use std::fs; imports filesystem module into the crate root, signaling I/O is part of this module's public API surface rather than being isolated in a shell layer
findings.failure_mode: module boundary pollution; callers may assume this module performs I/O when the core should be I/O-free
findings.fix: Move fs usage to a dedicated shell module. The core module should have no std::fs imports

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16. Value has domain invariants (range 0..=65535, likely non-negative). No domain newtype or value object for name or value
findings.failure_mode: illegal values can be constructed at any call site without domain validation at construction
findings.fix: Create newtype wrappers like RecordName(String) with a fallible constructor, and use u16 directly as value type with validation

findings.problem: No error type defined. Function returns Vec<Record> with no Result, so all errors are panics. No domain error taxonomy for I/O failures vs parse failures
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot distinguish between file-not-found, permission-denied, malformed line, out-of-range value, or missing fields
findings.fix: Define enum SessionLoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Parse { line: usize, field: &'static str, reason: String } } and return Result<Vec<Record>, SessionLoadError>

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or memory usage
no profiler data for allocation patterns (intermediate Vec<String> per line, repeated to_string)
no allocation audit - try_reserve not used, no capacity tracking for large files
no second-ring review artifact (no proof plan, no black-hat review, no formal verification)
no behavior tests or integration tests for malformed input handling
no command evidence (no cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy run results)
residual_risk: This is a static review only with no commands run. The code has 8 BLOCKER violations (unwrap/panic on I/O and parse, unchecked indexing, lossy cast, hidden I/O in core, missing split_once, wrong parse target type, missing try_reserve) plus 5 WARNING/INFO issues. The functional core/imperative shell boundary is entirely violated - the single function performs filesystem I/O, console I/O, and data parsing. Every error path panics. The code is not safe for any untrusted input.
